resources.string: Experimental DirtyFrag build for %1$s on %2$s. Choose a backend, then root — no Shizuku needed. These builds still need testing on your phone. Changing an active backend requires a full reboot. Existing modules are disabled when changing backends; re-enable compatible modules in the chosen manager.

Experimental build for SM-S948B on S948BXXS4AZHL. Choose a backend, then start Shizuku through wireless debugging before rooting. These builds still need testing on your phone. Changing an active backend requires a full reboot. Existing modules are disabled when changing backends; re-enable compatible modules in the chosen manager.
Open the app and choose a root backend before starting.
%1$s selected for the next root attempt.
%1$s selected. Reboot before starting the new backend.
Disable existing modules before loading. Re-enable compatible modules in the selected manager. Backend changes always disable existing modules.
Always loads the selected backend during rooting.
Marks boot, vbmeta and related partitions read-only once bootstrap root is verified, until reboot. Flashing tools and some installers stop working while it is on.
Reset all root state before loading

Recovery only: deletes everything under /data/adb (modules, manager data, staged metamodule copies) before the backend loads, then must be turned off again. On DirtyFrag runs only module state is cleared before loading — manager data and su grants are kept — and the wipe is skipped while a backend is already live, so reboot first.

The next run will permanently delete everything under /data/adb, including all modules, Mountify data and manager module state, before loading the backend. Reinstall what you need afterwards, then turn this off again.
